mstts:express-as.prosody: Welcome—I'm so glad you're here with me. Imagine a time when restlessness and uncertainty are in the air, when the world you thought you knew is shifting beneath your feet. That's the 1960s in America, where searching for meaning gets tangled up with the unraveling of old rules and expectations. Together, we're about to explore all of this through the eyes of Joan Didion, in her remarkable work, Slouching Towards Bethlehem. She takes us right into the heart of California—where the sunlit promise of the West Coast is shadowed by disillusionment, and where the ordinary and extraordinary seem to collide in unexpected ways. Through personal stories and big public moments, Didion reveals just how complex our sense of identity, morality, and belonging can be. We'll meet characters who are searching for authenticity, feeling the tension between freedom and responsibility, and wrestling with that quiet ache of not quite fitting in. What if you could see the world as both beautiful and bewildering—marked by flashes of hope, yet haunted by doubts? As we wander through this tapestry of vivid portraits and sharp observations, you might start to notice how culture shapes us, even as we shape it—how the familiar fades into the unfamiliar, blurring the lines between ourselves and the world around us. So, as we begin this journey together, let’s stay curious. We’ll look for meaning in the chaos, and maybe, just maybe, discover something about finding our own place when everything feels up in the air. Ready to dive in? Let’s get started.
